newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Unimarc whets investor appetites.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Unimarc whets investor appetites.

text.p: Chilean supermarket chain Supermercados Unimarc SA stormed up in its debut in Santiago and New York as investors rushed to grab a share of the country's booming retail business, said analysts.
"It's a very attractive sector for investors who are keen to diversify their portfolios," said Paula del Sol, an analyst at Santander Investment.
"The outlook is good as the industry will benefit from the end of Chile's economic adjustment and from the growth expected this year."
The consumer sector has been the most sensitive to Chile's belt-tightening imposed by the Central Bank over a year ago to slow galloping economic growth.

Unimarc, Chile's 20th company to trade publicly on Wall Street, charged to $18 per American Depositary Receipt (ADR) within minutes of its launch at $16.75. In Santiago, stock which was priced at a minimum 140 pesos started trading at 150 pesos. Investors have been clearing Santa Isabel SA -- the only other Chilean supermarket to have issued ADRs -- from their portfolios to make room for Unimarc, said analysts.
"This explains why Santa Isabel has fallen in the last few weeks," said one trader.
Although supermarkets are among the Santiago bourse's favorite stocks, tough competition in the industry has started to worry investors, said del Sol.
Unimarc, Santa Isabel, and another chain, D&S, have plans to invest hundreds of million of dollars building dozens of new stores which could swamp the already well-developed Chilean market.
"Not all the projects are viable. This is concern for the sector," she said.

Chileans are Latin America's most enthusiastic supermarket shoppers with over 90 percent of domestic shopping in Santiago carried out in supermarket stores, said to be the highest rate in any major Latin American city, analysts have said.
The sharp opening rally may have brought Unimarc's shares close to their market value, said analysts CB Capitales, which classified the stock as "hold."
"The recommendation is based on the fact that the company's expansion plan is based on the segment of the market with the lowest growth outlook," said CB Capitales in a report.

"Unimarc's projects are aimed at increasing its presence in the high price, high service sector of the market -- the most profitable in the industry, but the one which offers the lowest rates of future growth."
Other traders were more optimistic, expecting Unimarc and Santa Isabel to be among the sector's top stock gainers this year.
Unimarc and Santa Isabel, which are both trading at P/E ratios of around 15, are likely to catch up with D&S, which is already selling at 21, said one dealer.
"No doubt Santa Isabel has been hurt recently by Unimarc's arrival, but there is no doubt that both will have P/E ratios near 20," he said.
